A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRESELECT study. All 22 pages of v3 and 24 pages of v4, including Appendices A–C, support comparison. Text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-pretraining experiments on RefinedWeb and C4, downstream evaluations in Tables 1–2 and Appendix C, and analyses of selected data and classifier features.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds a ScalingFilter comparison and target-ranking sensitivity results in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: The proposed six-model rank-matching score, positive/negative document selection, and fastText filtering pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 investigates alternative scoring configurations without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix A.7.2 adds evaluation of losses on wiki-related raw texts; v3's reported raw-text loss evaluations covered Math and Code. The RefinedWeb and C4 training coverage and established downstream benchmark suites remain unchanged.

E2.justification: ScalingFilter becomes an evaluated comparator in v4 Appendix A.7.1 and Table 7. Both Perplexity Correlation variants, DD and DP, already participated in v3 Table 1; their clearer appendix labeling does not introduce additional comparators.

E3.justification: v4 newly reports a HellaSwag-based versus average-performance target-ranking experiment at 400M parameters and 8B training tokens. It also specifies a two-scorer ScalingFilter comparison under the existing 1B/30B setting. The original experiments' budgets, architectures, and evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 substantially expands scrutiny of the selection design: it compares two-model ScalingFilter with six-model PRESELECT, analyzes their score relationship and selected-document characteristics, and tests sensitivity to the target ranking. These address design questions beyond v3's descriptive feature, domain, and length analyses. Figures 5–6 also extend the positive/negative seed-data analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix A.7.1 introduces Spearman and Pearson correlation estimation between ScalingFilter scores and PRESELECT predictive strength on sampled documents. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental performance results.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are unchanged. New Table 7 reports ScalingFilter at 37.6 alongside retained Random 37.2 and PRESELECT 40.3 averages. A.7.1 adds correlations of 0.0533 and -0.079 and a 2300-character selected-text average. A.7.2 reports 5% lower wiki losses and 8%/16% higher Math/Code losses for the target-ranking variant. Figures 5–6 add seed-domain percentages.

T1.justification: The predictive-strength definition in Equation 1 and fastText feature-contribution derivation in Appendix A.3 remain unchanged. The new discussion contrasting loss differences with rank alignment supplies interpretation, without adding formal definitions, proofs, or derived guarantees.

C1.justification: The predictive-data hypothesis, lightweight document-selection contribution, downstream-performance claims, and 10x training-compute claim retain their meaning. The shortened conclusion and more prominent acknowledgment of Thrush et al. do not redefine contributions already qualified in v3's introduction.

C2.justification: v4 newly interprets the ScalingFilter comparison as evidence for intermediate scoring models and the target-ranking experiment as evidence of ability-specific selection beyond training scale. Appendix A.7.3 explicitly acknowledges selection of adult content and proposes separate rule-based filtering, without reporting a tested mitigation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 documents the Llama-65B/Llama-7B scorer pair for ScalingFilter and the training scales of the added analyses. The corpus table explicitly lists the already evaluated DP baseline. Existing fastText settings, feature adjustment, hardware, computation-overhead estimates, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to ScalingFilter, Marion et al. (2023), and Ankner et al. (2024), extending discussion of perplexity-based selection. The abstract and introduction more explicitly acknowledge Thrush et al.'s preceding hypothesis, although v3 already discussed that relationship extensively.

P1.justification: Changes include localized abstract/introduction edits, compressed related-work headings and conclusion, new Appendix A.7 subsections and cross-references, and acknowledgments and an impact statement. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds two seed-domain bar charts and the ScalingFilter comparison table, and expands the corpus table with a DP row. Existing domain-distribution Figures 5–6 become Figures 7–8 without changed graphical content. The established layout remains; the new charts' Top-10 captions inconsistently accompany 15 displayed domains.

improvement.justification: The added comparator and target-ranking analysis provide useful scrutiny of PRESELECT, while clearer prior-work attribution and explicit sensitive-content discussion improve transparency. These are limited gains over the retained experimental foundation. In particular, ScalingFilter changes both the scoring rule and scorer count, so its comparison does not isolate the benefit of intermediate models, and uncertainty in the added experimental differences remains unquantified.
